item.title: IFA says outbreak of bluetongue 'must not derail cattle trade'
item.description: The IFA says Ireland's first outbreak of bluetongue must not derail the cattle trade. A case of the virus has been identified on a cattle farm in east Wexford. The Agriculture Minister says it will have a knock-on effect on live exports, with additional costs and logistical issues required depending on the country of destination. President of the Irish Farmers' Association, Francie Gorman says the outbreak needs to be contained immediately: Advertisement

item.title: Tree down on Crossdoney Road outside Ballinagh
item.description: Motorists in Ballinagh, Co. Cavan are urged to be careful on the Crossdoney Road just outside the village. Gardaí have confirmed a tree is down on the road and is obstructing traffic. The tree is currently in the process of being cleared, but drivers are reminded to exercise extra caution in the area this morning. Advertisement

item.title: Work 'only beginning' for special school in Castleblayney
item.description: The work is only beginning for the special school in Castleblayney. That's according to Local Minister of State, Niamh Smyth, who visited the school with Education Minister Hildegarde Naughton this week. She outlined that the school has been "a long time coming" but that it is only the beginning of the journey. Minister Smyth highlighted that parents have called for a bigger, permanent school. Speaking to Northern Sound, she said that there is still "a lot of work to be done." Advertisement Mean

item.title: Local senator says sheep worrying is on the rise
item.description: Local Senator Robbie Gallagher has said that the trend of dogs attacking livestock and sheep is "only going up". Senator Gallagher raised the issue in the Seanad this week. item.title: Local councillor condemns far-right protest in Co. Cavan
item.description: A local councillor has condemned a far-right protest which took place in Co. Cavan yesterday. The gathering in Drumalee promoted Zionism and participants, who were of Eastern European descent, claimed they were neo-Nazis. According to Sinn Féin councillor Stiofán Conaty, attendees were asked why they were displaying Israeli flags, following which a violent altercation ensued. He says all political opinions are welcome, but a line must be drawn on hateful ideologies: Advertisement

item.title: Documents prepared to appoint design consultant to St Tiernach's Park project
item.description: A local councillor has highlighted the importance of "keeping the foot on the pedal" when it comes to development works at St Tiernach's Park in Clones.
